reason: Calling ProvDocument.deserialize with the format name nope raises DoNotExist. The Raises section of prov.serializers.get, which docs/reference/serializers.md renders, says DoNotExist is raised for an unregistered format, and the exception tree there lists DoNotExist.

Deserialising each malformed fixture file with its explicit format raises the library's own error for ill-formed syntax (`JSONDecodeError`, `XMLSyntaxError`, `BadSyntax`), `ProvJSONException` for well-formed JSON of the wrong shape (#228) and `ProvXMLException` for a foreign root that holds a child. docs/reference/serializers.md says input not well-formed in the underlying syntax raises the parsing library's own error. A proposal to drop the row xml-wrong-root, which reads an `<html>` root in no namespace with a child, was refuted. That row passes the root through `_adopt_own_default` and raises from the namespace check in the loop of `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree`. test_xml.py::test_non_prov_top_level_element_raises reads a `prov:document` root with a foreign-namespace child, so it never meets a foreign root. A fault in `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize`, placed before `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree` runs, that returns an empty document for any root outside the PROV namespace fails this row and passed the whole suite with the row deselected (5302 passed). The fault is plausible because it extends to every foreign root the leniency that test_malformed.py::test_xml_childless_foreign_root_parses_to_empty_document pins for a childless one. A second fault, which makes the loop of `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree` skip a child in no namespace, also fails the row and passed the whole suite with the row deselected. Keep every row.

Reading an empty Turtle file with the rdf format returns a document with no records and raises nothing. This test asserts that the reader does not raise, so its rejecting rules are the contract (rule 6): the empty-input rows json-empty and xml-empty of test_malformed.py::test_malformed_file_raises raise, and docs/reference/serializers.md says input that is not well-formed raises the parsing library's own error, and an empty Turtle file is well-formed.

Reading Turtle that holds only foaf triples warns with a UserWarning whose message says not converted and returns a document with no records. The PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md says a subject typed with no PROV class gets no record and one ProvWarning lists such subjects, and the ProvWarning docstring says a reader's skip warning is also a UserWarning.

Calling prov.read on a path to a file of prose raises TypeError. The exception tree in docs/reference/serializers.md makes ProvFormatNotDetected also a TypeError, and prov.read raises it when no candidate format reads the source (#239).

Reading an XML file whose only content is a childless foreign root element foo returns a document with no records and raises nothing. This test asserts that the reader does not raise, so its rejecting rule is the contract (rule 6): a foreign root that holds a child raises ProvXMLException, as the row xml-wrong-root of test_malformed.py::test_malformed_file_raises pins.
